prompt: Objective: decide whether to buy a competitor for $400M. What you've learned: the target is worth about $350M on its own. Latest finding: cost synergies are estimated at $30M a year. What is the best next step?

options.text: Check how much the two companies' customers overlap
options.feedback: Useful later for revenue risks, but the deal turns on value against price.

options.text: Estimate revenue synergies on top of the cost savings
options.feedback: Secondary: first check whether the cost synergies already justify the price.

options.text: Check whether net synergies justify the $400M price
options.feedback: Right. $350M stand-alone is $50M short of the price. The deal works only if the synergies, net of integration costs, close that gap.

options.text: Re-estimate the target's stand-alone value with a second method

explanation: Stand-alone value is $350M against a $400M price. The question is whether $30M a year of synergies, net of integration costs, closes the gap.
